To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the histone modifications, H3K27me3, ubH2B, H3K9me2, and H3K9ac are associated with the IRF1 locus in the unstimulated state.
histone modification at the IRF-1 promoter is dynamic and correlates with interferon (γIFN) induction of STAT-1 activity.

the histone modifications H3K4 trimethylation, H3K27 acetylation and H2B monoubiqitination are dynamic during interferon γ (IFNγ)-mediated activation of the IRF1 locus and that the recruitment of MEN1 and RNF20 is associated with the dynamic histone modifications at IRF1.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the role of histones in transcriptional control, and how histone modifications regulate STAT activation of the IRF1 transcriptional program.
the role of histones and chromatin in the regulation of gene expression, specifically the role that histone modifications play during the activation of transcription by STAT1.
the dynamic nature of histone modifications during the activation of gene expression and how these modifications are regulated to control transcription.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

histone modification dynamics are important for gene transcription and that the recruitment of histone modifiers, such as RNF20, to the chromatin is important for the proper execution of STAT1 signaling and the control of IFNγ-induced gene transcription.
H2B ubiquitination and H3K36 methylation are associated with transcriptional repression, but that H3K4 and H3K79 methylation are associated in part with transcriptional activation.
the dynamics of histone modifications and the localization of COMPASS- and RNF20-associated complexes are important in the transcriptional regulation of STAT-activated genes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
STAT1-mediated gene activation is associated with dynamic and transient chromatin modifications that are critical for the proper execution of transcription.
STAT1 activation of IRF1 gene expression requires a dynamic histone modification landscape, which involves the recruitment of MEN1 and RNF20 to the gene locus.

STAT1-mediated transcription of the IRF1 locus is regulated by a dynamic balance of histone modifications and the recruitment of chromatin modifying proteins, such as RNF20, which in turn, affects Pol II CTD cycling.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the histone code at a gene locus is dynamic and that the dynamics of histone modifications are important for the regulation of STAT1-activated gene expression.
the dynamics of histone modification are essential for the regulation of STAT-activated transcription of the IRF1 locus.
histone modifications and their associated proteins play a critical role in the regulation of STAT1-activated gene transcription.
